e-4711.knowledge_point: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination
e-4711.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079703/assets/a50d551e5d8abe8d9ae48778b195c382bbbf96f6fc5083c41b67642e99deffda.png)
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
e-4711.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079703/assets/48c423256fbdc0d7e4f6ff716fb449efe6f98bdf57ba90353bcced930ea4ed17.png)

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079703/assets/81b7626ac30b06c5eeb10be274dd93476a86dce5fe3053722d96e16b78d7f165.png)

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $z,$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $z$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1-5y \\ y=y \\ z=3,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1-5y \\ y \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

e-6173.knowledge_point: Classifying a System as Consistent Dependent, Consistent Independent, or Inconsistent
e-6173.problem:
Given the system
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079703/assets/427c19efbebba6bfe2dc36bccd852d7a1f5e0ec97dc46c00043d019807e86ec2.png)
which of the following statements are true?

- The system is consistent dependent

- The system has no solution

- The system is consistent independent
e-6173.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079703/assets/50f13deaa03c2af30f511ef3d514e3dd2e118d81d9b121b436ff1a2f2497c303.png)

Using Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -4 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079703/assets/e02bb5004f792eea20216e64098bb924dbed15defb9330967d6ae5a144e067dc.png)

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
2x -3y= 4
$$

The basic variable is $x,$ and we have a free variable $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*.

As a result, only statement I is true.

e-4712.knowledge_point: Determining the Value of a Constant for Which a Given Linear System Is Consistent or Inconsistent
e-4712.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-2y=1, \\ 4x+ky=-3\end{aligned}
$$
e-4712.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079703/assets/f4478e5828da7c79a47bf3ca212ed15357befe7b0b208c78beb0895b445272c9.png)

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & k & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & k+4 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079703/assets/cfea36ae2b5cb5d8715480c1e0ee0b5ba06cf39d0c2032eb6e9b9078bf8c5bde.png)

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=-4,$ then the second equation is $0=-5,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=-4.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

No solution
b
[3x3+11−5x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
c
[1−3x31−5x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
d
[3x3−15x3+1x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
e

decision.explanation: The augmented matrix is [[1,-1,2,2],[1,0,-3,1]]. Apply R2 := R2-R1, then R1 := R1+R2 to obtain RREF [[1,0,-3,1],[0,1,-5,-1]]. Thus x1=3x3+1 and x2=5x3-1, with x3 any real number. This is option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now  

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=1 \\  & {x}_{2}-5{x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=3{x}_{3}+1 \\ {x}_{2}=5{x}_{3}-1 \\ {x}_{3}={x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3}+1 \\ 5{x}_{3}-1 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

choices.html: No solution

Consider the system of linear equations {x1−x2+2x3=2x1−3x3=1. Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
No solution
b
[3x3+11−5x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
c
[1−3x31−5x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
d
[3x3−15x3+1x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
e
[3x3+15x3−1x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is
M=[1−12210−31].

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

M=[1−12210−31]R2:=R2−R1∼[1−12201−5−1]R1:=R1+R2∼[10−3101−5−1]

The corresponding system is now

{x1−3x3=1x2−5x3=−1.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x1 and x2, and we have one free variable, x3. That means we need to find x1 and x2 in terms of x3.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x1=3x3+1x2=5x3−1x3=x3,

where x3 (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

[x1x2x3]=[3x3+15x3−1x3],x3∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now  

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=1 \\  & {x}_{2}-5{x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=3{x}_{3}+1 \\ {x}_{2}=5{x}_{3}-1 \\ {x}_{3}={x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3}+1 \\ 5{x}_{3}-1 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=4 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

Question 2
?

Consider the system of linear equations {x1+2x2−2x3=4−2x1−3x2−2x3=−2. Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
[−8−8x36−6x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
b
[8−x33+3x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
c
[−8−10x36+6x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
d
[−8−x36+x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
e
[−8−6x310+6x3x3],x3∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R2 := R2+2R1 to the augmented matrix to get [0,1,-6,6] as the second row. Then R1 := R1-2R2 gives RREF [[1,0,10,-8],[0,1,-6,6]]. Hence x1=-8-10x3 and x2=6+6x3, with x3 any real number, so option c is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=4 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 10 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now  

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+10{x}_{3}=-8 \\  & {x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=-8-10{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2}=6+6{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}={x}_{3},\end{aligned}

$$

$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=4 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 10 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now  

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+10{x}_{3}=-8 \\  & {x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=-8-10{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2}=6+6{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}={x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8-10{x}_{3} \\ 6+6{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the system of linear equations {2x−4z=24x+y−5z=4. Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
[1+2z−3zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
b
[2+4z1−3zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
c
[2+4z−3zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
d
[−2z4zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
e
[1+4z3zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Starting with [[2,0,-4,2],[4,1,-5,4]], apply R1 := R1/2 and R2 := R2-4R1. The RREF is [[1,0,-2,1],[0,1,3,0]], giving x=1+2z and y=-3z, with z any real number. This matches option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-4z=2 \\ 4x+y-5z=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2z=1 \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+2z \\ y=-3z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1+2z \\ -3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-4z=2 \\ 4x+y-5z=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2z=1 \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+2z \\ y=-3z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1+2z \\ -3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations {x−2y+2z=2y−z=−1. Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
[−zz−1z],z∈(−∞,∞)
b
[−1−zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
c
[1−z0z],z∈(−∞,∞)
d
[0z−1z],z∈(−∞,∞)
e
[2−z0z],z∈(−∞,∞)

decision.explanation: The augmented matrix is [[1,-2,2,2],[0,1,-1,-1]]. Applying R1 := R1+2R2 gives RREF [[1,0,0,0],[0,1,-1,-1]]. Thus x=0 and y=z-1, with z any real number, matching option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+2z=2 \\  & y-z=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x=0 \\  & y-z=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=0 \\ y=z-1 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ z-1 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+2z=2 \\  & y-z=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x=0 \\  & y-z=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=0 \\ y=z-1 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ z-1 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

c

decision.explanation: Apply R1 := R1/2, then R1 := R1-R2. The augmented matrix becomes RREF [[1,0,0,4],[0,1,2,-6]]. Thus x1=4 and x2=-6-2x3, with x3 any real number, matching option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=-4 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now   

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}=4 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ Since we have that ${x}_{1}=4$,  we only need to find ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=4 \\ {x}_{2}=-6-2{x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=-4 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now   

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}=4 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ Since we have that ${x}_{1}=4$,  we only need to find ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=4 \\ {x}_{2}=-6-2{x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

- The system is consistent dependent
- The system is inconsistent

after.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 6 \\ 2 & -3 & 13 \\ 5 & -1 & 45\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 6 \\ 2 & -3 & 13 \\ 5 & -1 & 45\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 25 \\ 5 & -1 & 45\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 25 \\ 0 & 9 & 75\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-9){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 25 \\ 0 & 0 & -150\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y=-150,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement II is true.

{\begin{aligned} & x+4y=-1 \\  & 2x+8y=-2 \\  & -3x-12y=3\end{aligned}

- The system is inconsistent
- The system is consistent dependent

after.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 8 & -2 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 8 & -2 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x,$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we can find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*. 

As a result, only statement II is true.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+4y=12 \\  & x+ky=4\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 12 \\ 1 & k & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 12 \\ 1 & k & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & k & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & k & 4 \\ 0 & 4-3k & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+ky=4 \\  & (4-3k)y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=\frac{4}{3},$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$, and we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $x+ky=4.$ 

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=\frac{4}{3}.$

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y=-4 \\  & 3x+2ky=-2\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & 2k & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & 2k & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 2k-6 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y=-4 \\ (2k-6)y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=3,$ then the second equation is $0=10,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=3.$

after.html:
Question 13
?

Determine the value of k for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

{x+2y=−43x+2ky=−2

a
 k=−1
b
 k=−2
c
 k=−3
d
 k=3
e
 k=2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is

M=[12−432k−2].

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

M=[12−432k−2]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[12−402k−610]

The corresponding system is now

{x+2y=−4(2k−6)y=10.

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If k=3, then the second equation is 0=10, which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when k=3.

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Value of a Constant for Which a Given Linear System Is Consistent or Inconsistent
content.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y=-4 \\  & 3x+2ky=-2\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & 2k & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & 2k & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 2k-6 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y=-4 \\ (2k-6)y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=3,$ then the second equation is $0=10,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=3.$

a

 k=−4

 k=4
d

e

decision.explanation: Subtracting twice the first equation from the second gives (k+2)y=-2. This becomes the contradiction 0=-2 exactly when k=-2. Therefore option e is correct.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-y=3 \\  & 4x+ky=4\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & k & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & k & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & k+2 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-y=3 \\  & (k+2)y=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

Now if $k=-2$, then the second equation is $0=-2,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when  $k=-2.$
